text: Running over, you fill all the space around you, since relying on yourself is what feels safe. Help never gets a turn, and the weight stays with you.

Spending it all is your first instinct. Money left to sit feels like a chance going cold, and you spend it all on the next thing rather than keep it. Remember that you are allowed to let money sit until the right chance comes.

Doing a thing the usual way is nearly impossible for you, and only an original one feels done. Taking it apart first, you make your own version rather than follow the rule. Your work carries a mark nobody else could have left.

You share each win rather than sit on it. Giving in bursts is your way of loving, and you hand the people around you plenty one year and nothing the next. Nobody near you ever doubts where your heart is.

You push back before you hear the end of a plan. To you, being hard to convince feels like being hard to fool, and you make people defend a plan instead of taking it. You take the ease out of every offer they bring you.

You prove an idea before you share it. Because you would rather show a result than explain a plan, you keep people out of it until it is done. Those close to you meet the work at the end and miss the making of it.

When a rule stops making sense, you rewrite it with people still standing on it. Since you fix it rather than keep the peace, you change the footing with no warning. The rule you found pointless was somebody's floor.
As a catalyst, the gate opens late. Nothing of yours comes through until it is ready, and then it comes out blunt and complete.
As a friction, the holding never stops. Familiar ground draws you in, every change looks like a threat, and your life grows smaller each year.

Second-guessing an answer you already have leaves people waiting on it. Because being certain comes first, you sit on the yes or no for weeks rather than give a maybe. You stall their next step for as long as you second-guess.

Pushing through, you carry the people with you at your pace. You would rather keep your speed than slow it for someone, and that costs them the pause you never take. With you at the front, the group finishes what it started.

Earth runs through your wealth, your family and your social life. It is the chance you spot while it is still far off, the good year that becomes a gift for everyone at home, and the luck you hand round before it has cooled.

Earth runs through your wealth, your family and your career. It is the money put by that makes a bad month ordinary, the old chair you fix instead of buying a new one, and the job you see through to a proper finish.

Earth runs through your mind, your growth and your career. It is the idea you work out in your own strange way, the skill you picked up without a teacher and kept to yourself, and the meaning you catch under the words in a meeting.

Seek Wood, your own Body energy. Wood is the trunk under everything you reach for, the body that stands before it carries. Let it hold what Earth piles up. Your load has grown past what you can bear alone. Start each week with one thing that is only for you. Say no to one request before you say yes again.
Spending on the people you love comes no easier than spending on yourself. Giving less feels safer than giving more, and you cut back on them first. You take what you save out of their share.

Because you do better with a rival, you turn a peer into one without asking. You would rather race someone than keep them company, and you hand a contest to a friend who wanted none. Your friends get faster just from standing next to you.

Earth runs through your family, your social life and your career. It is the promise at home kept without a reminder, the decision both sides of an argument can live with, and the work left in your hands because you never let it slip.

Without an audience, you will not start. Practising alone feels like wasted effort, and you save the real work for a crowd rather than do it unseen. You lose the quiet practice that your talent needs most to grow.

You overdo it, and you know it while you do. Since enough never feels like a real amount to you, you push a thing past its best rather than stop there. You are allowed to stop where a thing is at its best.

You think fast enough to finish other people's sentences, and often you do. Waiting for a thought to end feels like wasted time, and you answer before hearing it all. Slower thinkers lose the last part of their point to your reply.

You trust closeness only side by side, so you let a friend near once they match your pace. You would rather keep your footing than be carried, even when you need it. On your hard days, nobody is close enough to catch you.

Your Body is the strength the whole of you stands on. Fire makes it warm, so you recover by doing. Running thin, the reserve goes first, because you keep moving instead of stopping to refill. You pay for each bright day with a tired one.
As a catalyst, little teaching reaches you. You feed on what you find by yourself, and insight arrives in flashes with nobody there to share it.

Your Mind is where the world soaks in and becomes yours. Fire makes it warm, and you keep what lights you up. As a catalyst, little warmth or teaching reaches you. You learn to manage without it, and what you understand you reached on your own.

Your Mind grows on warmth, and warmth is something you have to go and sit near. Once a month, go to a talk or a workshop just to take it in. Choose one person to ask the simple questions, and ask them.

Your first read of anyone is a kind one. Because you would rather keep a person warm than judge them out loud, you hold back the truth they needed. You leave them with your warmth and without your honest view.
You look after people without being asked. Keeping the people near you sheltered is how you feel at ease, so you put their comfort before yours. Under your roof, everyone breathes out.

The care you give so freely is also the care you lean on in return. Because another person's steadiness feels more reliable than yours, you lean on theirs rather than build your own. You go without the one kind of strength you cannot borrow.

Each time a loved one is about to fail, you step in. Protecting them from the consequence feels more like love to you than letting them meet it. With every rescue, you keep from them the small win of managing on their own.

Seek Earth, the Mind energy. Earth takes the blaze in and keeps the warmth, soil that does not catch. Let it ground what Fire burns. You answer to pressure faster than you recover from it. Stay with one hard feeling for ten minutes before you act on it. Tend one plant or one friendship with no goal attached.
Being in charge weighs on you once you take it. You feel safer running things alone than sharing them, so you are rarely carried. Nobody thinks to ask how you are holding up.

Where the book and your judgment part, you side with the book. You want it done in order more than your way, so you let the book overrule what you already knew. Chances that needed a quick call pass you by.
You trust a thing only when it is done by the book. Since an outside rule steadies you, you go by the book over the shortcut. Your work is the standard others get checked against.
Keeping a thing going is the warmest part of you. You would rather keep one thing warm for years than start many, since what lasts feels real to you. Your oldest friendships still hold.

Your Action is what you go and build, claim and provide. Fire turns it bright, lit the moment a chance appears. As a friction, the light burns through its fuel. Gain and loss fill your thoughts, and little of you is left to rest.
As a friction, the line cuts deeper than any task asks, because easing off feels unsafe. You wear out long before the work does.
Off duty is a state you never fully manage. The alert in you never stands down, and you spend a free evening on duty rather than inside it. You lose the rest your evenings off were meant to give you.
As a catalyst, the line runs faint and you draw it yourself. You built your standing one rule after another.
Properly is the one speed you own. You do every step properly rather than good enough, and small tasks take the care big ones deserve. Your evenings go to jobs that nobody would ever check.
As a friction, you claim far more than you see through. Your freedom lives in the next chance, and the one in hand rarely pays off.

Seek Fire, your own Body energy. Fire is warmth kept in, the fuel and rest that keep a light lit before it works on anything. Let it hold what Metal spends. You spend your strength on your claims, not yourself, and tired is where you make your worst deals. Eat warm food daily. Talk deals through with a friend.

Playing it safe keeps you out of the loss column and the win column. You take the known small wage rather than the unknown better one, since playing safe is never judged. You pay for playing it safe in the chance you watched others take.

You spot the opening when it is only a gap. You wake more for a far chance than a near one, and you spot a newer opening while you are claiming this one. Your eye finds a door where everyone else sees a wall.

Setting the bar is something you do unasked. A standard you did not choose bores you, so you set your own rather than keep the given one, and hold yourself to it. Anything you finish has already passed the hardest judge it will meet.

Whenever someone tries to teach you, you check the messenger first. Since being right is how you stay safe, you defend your position rather than learn from theirs. You lose every lesson that needed you to be wrong before it could teach you.
Running over, your will needs a contest and finds one wherever you go. Wanting to know where you stand costs you the company you came for.

Where the bet is biggest, you are calmest, and you take that as a sign. Trusting nerve more than numbers, you bet with the rent before the sums are done. You come out of that calm short on rent and short on sleep.

Recovering alone spares the people near you your worst days. You return recovered rather than be seen recovering, and give them the finished version only. Your closest people meet you only on your good days.

You treat rest as something you earn after the work instead of the thing the work runs on. Cut one commitment this month that drains more than it gives. Decide your stopping time before you start, and stop there.

Protective is your instinct with the people you love. You need them safe more than you need them tested, so you step in before letting them fall. You are protecting them from the one thing that would have taught them.

Your thinking stays private until it is done. Working it out alone comes easier to you than working it out together, and the people near you get only the conclusion. They meet your plans finished, with no part in the making of them.

Keeping it in keeps it from being judged. Inside is where an idea stays safe, and you hold yours back until it is perfect rather than let it out rough. You go unheard on the very things you understand best.

Your Mind takes in less than it could use. Ask one person who knows more than you and wait for the whole reply. Take one free course on a subject that is new to you. Leave one hard question open for a week before you answer it.

Water runs through your mind, your growth and your career. It is the question you keep asking after the easy answer has come, the skill you learned your own way and own for good, and the read you have on someone before the handshake ends.

Seek Wood, the Mind energy. Wood is fuel that grows: it drinks the rain and turns it into something a fire can burn. Let it use what Water pours on you. You take every rule to heart faster than you take anything in. Start one project of your own this month. Learn one skill no rule asks for.
Your Order is the rules you answer to and the rank you hold by them. Water keeps it deep, and rules sink in to stay. As a friction, the rules outweigh what you want. You give up ease to keep them.

You do your best work with a date on it and someone waiting at the other end. Ask for honest feedback on one thing you made and just listen. Learn how one new task is done before you start on it. Leave an hour empty between two big jobs.

Slowly earned trust is the only trust you believe. You would rather earn trust over a year than win it in a day, since quick trust feels false. Work that needed you this month goes to someone with an easier smile.
As a friction, your Action moves on quicker than it settles. Each opening pulls you on before the last one pays.

Sleeping on a choice keeps your money safe, and it makes you late. You wait a night before saying yes, since a wrong yes costs more than a slow one. Bargains often go to whoever answered while you were still weighing it up.

Saving first hands your people the careful version of you. You put the savings before the trip together, and give them caution instead of company. The holidays they hoped to take with you stay in the planning.
You show up every day the same way, noticed or not. You value being counted on over being exciting, and you show up on dull days too. Whole teams quietly lean on you without saying so.

Your Action grows when it has somewhere to go and something to bring back. Put one plan into motion this season, a trip booked or a small venture opened with money you can spare. Follow one lead you heard about and see what it turns up.
As a friction, you spend care faster than it refills, because being needed feels like safety. By evening little is left for your own plans.

Seek Earth, the Mind energy. Earth is the ground under the water, the bank that stills it until it clears. Let it hold what Water pours. You let it all out as it comes, and nothing stays in long enough to settle. Keep one piece of news to yourself for a week. Stick with one plan for a whole month.

With whoever is in charge, you pick fights as your own kind of honesty. Because you fight in public rather than in private, you cost the one above you their footing in front of others. You leave them no quiet way to answer you.
What you have to give runs short, and it counts for nothing until someone hears it. Tell one person a story with no lesson in it. Ask them what they took from it, and listen to the end.

Seek Earth, the Order energy. Earth is the bank: it gives moving water a path and a shore. Let it shape what your Water pours. You hold more than you move, and what you do not move turns into weight. Before Sunday, finish one job you have put off. Keep the same day each week for one steady task.

Whenever enough is not enough, you keep your partners running past their finish. You push for the next round before asking, and they put in more than they meant. You use up the break they had planned to take at the end.

Carrying your own weight is the first thing you do. Being a load on nobody feels like safety, and you carry what is yours rather than hand a corner to a peer. Nobody ever has to wonder whether you will do your share.

All in together means you take someone with you every time. You put up the shared stake before asking whose it was, and a partner carries losses they never signed for. Anyone in with you lives through each venture's lows as well as its highs.

Your Action is what you go and build, claim and provide. Water gives it a current, and you gain most on the move. In balance, the current moves at your pace. You go out after an opening and come back with something kept.

You hold people at a distance that feels polite from your side. Being left alone matters more than being reached for, and your friends stay at the door. With that distance, you cost them a friend they could have reached.

One standard for yourself means one standard for your friends. Staying the same matters more than meeting anyone halfway, and an off day gets no slack. In a hard week, the people close to you get no softer version of you.
You are the same person in any company. One standard for yourself keeps your footing, since a new shape for each group would cost you your measure. Friends never have to guess which you will turn up.

Thinking a question through means walking all the way round it first. Being certain weighs more with you than being quick, so you take one more angle rather than decide. You circle a question for weeks that a single choice would have closed.

Keeping it in feels safer than being half understood. The private version stays perfect while the spoken one takes its chances, so you say the smaller idea. You keep the idea whole and lose the one thing you wanted from it, being known.

When someone close to you grows slowly, you give them time instead of a push. Holding back feels more like respect than a nudge, and the nudge they need never comes. Your patience leaves them to find the hard part on their own.
As a friction, the demands outgrow your strength and the pressure turns inward. Even an hour of ease begins to feel unearned.

Faced with a person, you reach for the book as if they were a form. Because an exception feels like playing favourites, you hand someone the rule rather than a hearing. Wanting to be fair, you give them a page in place of yourself.

Spending on the people near you comes before your own next month. Because helping them feels better than holding on, you spend on their short weeks rather than a shared cushion. You spend the savings meant to carry all of you through a lean month.

You count as closely for those you love as for yourself. Since a cost stays with you longer than a pleasure, you count shared things aloud rather than let them pass. You take the small treats out of their days, one price at a time.

You put comfort first for those in your care too. You would rather see them happy now than stretched, and you pick the easy choice over the useful one. You trade the effort they would grow on for an hour of ease.

Stopping feels like disappearing, and making keeps you here. The joy for you is in the making, and you make something new instead of staying idle. Fine work of yours sits in drawers, unseen and unthanked.
Off script is how you stay interested. Sticking to a plan dulls your talent, and you head off script rather than see it through. Many of your best ideas end up half built and never shown whole.

Speaking up for someone who has not asked you to is a habit of yours. Because a wrong left standing bothers you more than overstepping, you say their piece ahead of them. Your voice fills the space their own words were meant for.
